pages.q: Is Kissimmee a good place to live if you rent?
pages.short: For a lot of renters, yes. Kissimmee sits on the northwest shore of Lake Tohopekaliga, has a lively historic downtown and lakefront park, and puts Walt Disney World and the rest of the Orlando area within driving distance. The tradeoffs are humid summers, tourist traffic at peak times and a lifestyle that mostly runs on a car.

p: Kissimmee is the largest city and the county seat of Osceola County, and it is one of the principal cities of the Orlando metro area. That means you get a real hometown with its own downtown, plus easy reach to the bigger job centers and attractions around Orlando.

Life near the water is a big draw. Lake Toho is the largest lake in Osceola County, and Kissimmee Lakefront Park, right next to historic downtown, has paved walking trails, bike paths, a fishing pier, a splash pad, picnic areas and a pavilion. Admission to the park is free.
bullets: Free Movie in the Park nights on the first Friday of each month from September through March
Bass fishing, kayaking and paddleboarding on Lake Toho
Shopping and dining at The Loop, at John Young Parkway and Osceola Parkway
Orlando International Airport about 40 minutes away by car

p: Humidity is high most of the year, so plan on running the AC. Tourism keeps the local economy busy, which also brings crowds and congestion during peak travel times. One listing site rates the Stillwater Lakes area as car dependent with minimal transit nearby, so plan on driving for most errands, with SunRail as an option for some trips north.

Stillwater Lakes is a brand new lakefront community at 2175 Easton Loop, near Lake Tohopekaliga, Partin Settlement Road and US 192. It has a pond with a walking path on site, a resort style pool and a grand clubhouse, with easy access to Orlando, Lake Nona and Walt Disney World. See current homes and pricing on the Stillwater Lakes guide page, or call the leasing team at 689 314 6918.

pages.q: Should I rent in Kissimmee or Orlando?
pages.short: It depends on where you work and how you like to live. Kissimmee gives you a lakeside hometown feel on Lake Toho with Orlando still within reach by car or SunRail. Orlando puts you closer to its downtown and its northern suburbs. Compare commute, total monthly cost and the community itself before you pick a city.

p: Kissimmee and Orlando are part of the same metro area, officially named the Orlando Kissimmee Sanford Metropolitan Statistical Area. Kissimmee is the county seat of Osceola County and sits on the northwest shore of Lake Tohopekaliga, while Orlando is the larger city to the north in Orange County.
bullets: Kissimmee may suit you if you want lake life, a historic downtown and quick reach to the Disney side of the region
Orlando may suit you if your job, classes or social life are mostly downtown or further north
Either way, test your commute at the hour you would actually drive it

p: SunRail, the regional commuter train, has stops in Kissimmee, including the Kissimmee Amtrak station, and runs north to Orlando stops such as Orlando Health, Church Street, LYNX Central and AdventHealth before continuing to Winter Park and beyond. For most daily errands, though, plan on driving. Orlando International Airport is about 40 minutes from Kissimmee by car.

Rent is only part of the picture. Add any required monthly fees, utilities, parking, pet costs and commute costs, then compare. A community that includes something you would otherwise pay for, like an internet package, can change the math.
Commute costs count too. A shorter drive saves gas and time every week, so put a rough monthly number on it for each address you compare.

Stillwater Lakes is in Kissimmee at 2175 Easton Loop, near Partin Settlement Road and US 192, with easy access to Orlando, Lake Nona and Medical City, and Walt Disney World. The website lists a cable and internet package as included. Current pricing and any specials are on the Stillwater Lakes guide page.

pages.q: What does months free mean on an apartment lease?
pages.short: A months free special lowers the total rent you pay over a lease. The community either waives one or more full months, or spreads the savings as a discount across several months. Your base rent usually stays the same on paper, which matters at renewal. Always ask exactly how the free rent is applied before you sign.

sections.h: The common ways it is applied
bullets: A full month waived, often the first month or a month later in the lease
A percentage off rent for several months, such as half off for a set number of months
A credit spread evenly across the whole lease, which lowers every payment a little
p: All three can add up to the same savings. The difference is timing: one hits your budget all at once, the others smooth it out.

sections.h: How to figure your real monthly cost
p: Take the base rent, multiply by the months in the lease, subtract the free rent, then divide by the number of months. For example, one free month on a 12 month lease means you pay for 11 of the 12 months, so your average is eleven twelfths of the base rent. Then add required monthly fees, since a rent special applies to rent and may not touch other charges.
Doing this math for every community you tour lets you compare offers on equal terms, rather than comparing a headline number with a base rent.

bullets: Does the special require a certain lease length?
Is it only for certain floor plans or buildings?
Do I owe back the free rent if I break the lease early?
Will my renewal be based on the base rent or the discounted average?

sections.h: Service and support animals in Florida
p: Assistance animals are not pets under fair housing rules. Under Florida law, a tenant with a disability related need for an emotional support animal may not be charged extra for that animal. If the disability or need is not obvious, a landlord may ask for reliable supporting information, such as a note from a licensed health care practitioner, but may not ask for a diagnosis or medical records. A registration, ID card or certificate bought online is not enough on its own. The tenant is still responsible for any damage the animal causes. The landlord may also ask for proof of licensing and vaccinations.
This is general information, not legal advice. Laws change, so check the current rules or ask a local attorney or legal aid office about your situation.

pages.q: How much income do I need to rent an apartment in Kissimmee?
pages.short: A common screening rule is that your household earns about three times the monthly rent before taxes, and a listing for Stillwater Lakes shows that rule based on total household income. Roommates can usually combine income. Confirm the exact requirement with the leasing team, since screening rules can change.

sections.h: How the rule of three works
p: Multiply the monthly rent by three. If your gross monthly income, before taxes, meets or beats that number, you generally qualify on income. Because the rule is tied to rent, picking a smaller plan or splitting a larger one with a roommate can change whether you qualify.

Some communities use a different multiple, count only verified income, or look at credit and rental history alongside income. Ask for the screening criteria in writing so you know exactly how your application will be judged before you pay to apply.

When the requirement is based on total household income, everyone on the lease can count toward it. That is why a two bedroom with two baths, split two ways, can be easier to qualify for than a one bedroom on a single income. Each roommate usually applies separately and is listed on the lease. Ask whether a guarantor is accepted if one roommate is new to the area or between jobs, and whether income from a job that starts soon can count with an offer letter.

A photo ID for every adult applicant

pages.q: Do I need renters insurance for an apartment in Florida?
pages.short: Florida has no statewide law that makes renters buy it, so whether it is required comes down to your lease. Even when it is optional, it is worth having: a renters policy can cover your belongings, your personal liability and extra living costs if a covered loss forces you out. Standard policies typically do not cover flood.

p: According to the Florida Department of Financial Services, renters insurance protects you against financial loss when your personal property is damaged or destroyed by a covered peril. A typical policy has three key parts.
bullets: Personal property, generally covered anywhere in the world, with special limits on items like jewelry and art
Liability, if you become legally responsible for someone else's injury or property damage
Additional living expenses, if you must live elsewhere after a covered loss

p: FEMA notes that standard renters insurance typically does not cover flood damage. Florida's insurance regulator says flood coverage may be added to a renters policy by endorsement, or bought as a separate policy. Through the National Flood Insurance Program, renters can insure their belongings, and a new policy generally takes effect 30 days after purchase, so do not wait until a storm is in the forecast.
Because flood and wind claims can work differently, read the declarations page of any policy you buy and ask the agent to explain what is and is not covered.

bullets: Get quotes from a few carriers or an independent agent
Ask whether the policy pays replacement cost or actual cash value
Check the deductible for wind and hurricane claims
Take a quick video of your belongings on move in day

pages.q: What should renters in Kissimmee know about hurricanes?
pages.short: Plan ahead, not the night before. Osceola County says residents typically will not need to evacuate, but you should sign up for local alerts and keep a supply kit with seven days of food per person. Consider renters insurance with flood coverage, and know that Florida law gives tenants options if a storm badly damages their home.

bullets: Sign up for Alert Osceola at alertosceola.org, or text alertosceola to 888777
Store a seven day supply of nonperishable food for each person, and rotate it every six months
Pack a NOAA weather radio, flashlight, batteries, first aid supplies and a can opener
Buy flood coverage early, since a new NFIP policy usually takes effect 30 days after purchase

p: Ready Osceola says county residents typically will not need to evacuate, but if an order is issued, follow your local officials. Not every shelter opens for every storm, so check readyosceola.org or local TV. Osceola County can open evacuation, medical needs and pet friendly shelters. If you are not in a flood prone area or a manufactured home, the county suggests staying with friends or family outside the affected area as a first option.

sections.h: Your rights if your home is damaged
p: Under Florida's landlord tenant law, if your home is damaged through no fault of yours and your use of it is substantially impaired, you may end the rental agreement and move out right away. Or you can move out of only the unusable part and have rent reduced by that part's fair rental value. Either way, you must be given a chance to collect your belongings when it is safe, or notice of a date within a reasonable time when you can.
This is general information, not legal advice. Laws change, so check the current rules or ask a local attorney or legal aid office about your situation.
At Stillwater Lakes, ask the leasing team how residents get storm updates and what to do with patio furniture before high winds. Call 689 314 6918.
Take photos of your home and belongings at the start of each storm season, and keep copies of your lease and insurance documents somewhere you can reach from your phone.

pages.q: Can I break my apartment lease early in Florida?
pages.short: Often, yes, but it costs something. Florida lets landlords offer an early termination option in a separate lease addendum you sign at the start. If you accepted it, the fee cannot be more than two months' rent, and you can be asked for no more than 60 days' notice. If you declined it, your lease terms decide what you owe.

sections.h: How Florida's early termination option works
p: Florida law allows a landlord to charge liquidated damages or an early termination fee only if both sides agreed to it when the lease was signed. You show your choice on a separate addendum with boxes to accept or decline. If you accept, the amount cannot exceed two months' rent, and the required notice cannot be more than 60 days before the date you plan to leave.

sections.h: If you did not sign that addendum
p: Then your lease and Florida law decide what you may owe, and it can be more than a flat fee. Read the lease carefully, and talk with the leasing team before you give notice so there are no surprises. If the amount is large or unclear, a local tenant attorney or legal aid office can explain your options.
This is general information, not legal advice. Laws change, so check the current rules or ask a local attorney or legal aid office about your situation.

How much notice do I need to give?

p: Pick a term that matches your real plans. A longer lease can come with a better offer, but only if you are confident you will stay.
